subject: CedarHealth follow-up: infra constraints, SSO/KMS/HSM and hosting path
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: infra constraints & hosting path

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on CedarHealth's compliance and operational constraints. I wanted to capture the items we heard and propose recommended next steps so your security and infra teams have something concrete to review.

Key constraints (as discussed)
- SSO: SAML 2.0 via Okta (IdP metadata will be provided by your infra team)
- Key management: requirement for customer-controlled keys with FIPS 140-2 / HSM-backed protection (vendor: Thales nShield)
- Logs: retention requirement of 7 years for audit; ability to export logs to customer SIEM (Splunk/QRadar)
- Data residency: production data must remain in US-only cloud regions; egress rules will be strict
- Network: strict allowlist only (no public inbound except specific endpoints)

High-level fit guidance from Redwood's side
- Hosted API (our public, multi-tenant endpoint): does NOT meet the HSM + extended retention requirements today — not a fit for this use case.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): potentially viable if we can bridge KMS/HSM requirements — this depends on whether Cedar can accept a cloud KMS or a partner-mediated HSM connection. Some customers can meet their HSM needs with a dedicated placement plus a vetted HSM gateway, but we need to validate vendor compatibility and latency.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): the cleanest match for HSM-backed keys and long-term log retention. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and configurable archival to customer storage for long retention.

What we can deliver quickly
- An evidence pack (SOC 2, network diagrams, retention options) — attached as a stub for now.
- A one-pager on HSM integration approaches (attached).
- A proposed agenda and attendees for an infra deep-dive meeting to map the technical gaps.

Requested items from CedarHealth to help us narrow the path
1) Confirm HSM vendor and a technical contact for them (name/email).
2) Share SAML IdP metadata or Okta admin contact to validate SSO flows.
3) Clarify whether Cedar requires keys to remain on-premises (appliance) vs. cloud-hosted HSM acceptable if customer-managed.
4) Any specific archival requirements for logs (format, encryption-at-rest expectations, access controls).

Proposed next step: schedule a 60-minute infra deep-dive with your security/infra team and our engineering lead (Marissa). We are available Wed 15 Dec 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 16 Dec 09:00–11:00 PT. Which slot works for you?

For visibility, I’ve CC'd Aditya (AE) and Marissa (Solutions) to coordinate the follow-up and the evidence pack. I’ll assemble a short decision memo after the deep-dive so it can go to your security board.

Attaching: redwood_hsm_integration_onepager.pdf (stub), redwood_evidence_pack_2026.zip (stub)

Thanks — look forward to the next steps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@cedarhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@cedarhealth.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: infra constraints & hosting path

Kimberly — thanks for the concise summary. This captures our needs well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- HSM vendor: confirmed Thales nShield (we manage on-prem appliances today). I'll put you in touch with our HSM admin once you confirm a meeting time.
- Retention: 7 years is non-negotiable for the logs we store for audit. We expect WAL-style audit logs and request that logs can be exported to our Splunk deployment on a nightly basis.
- SSO: Okta SAML metadata will be provided; we can also share a test Okta tenant if that helps validation.
- Network: we will require a private peering/VPN between CedarHealth and any dedicated or private deployment; public-hosted endpoints are not acceptable for production.

Two asks for Redwood: can you provide a short note on whether Dedicated with a cloud-managed KMS can meet our HSM controls (specifically around key custody and FIPS-backed operations), or whether Private is the only path that satisfies the audit committee? Also we need a ballpark delta in cost (monthly) between Dedicated and Private so procurement can budget ahead of the security board meeting on 20 Dec.

Availability: Wed 15 Dec 10:00 PT works for our infra lead. Please include your solutions/eng lead and anyone who can speak to KMS/HSM architecture.

Thanks,
Lisa Carter
Director, IT Security
CedarHealth
lisa.carter@cedarhealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: CedarHealth infra constraints — quick tech mapping

Kim / Marissa — quick technical mapping and recommended deliverables before Wed's deep-dive.

Technical mapping (short):
- Hosted API: fails on HSM key custody + private networking; rule this out for production. Good for pilot/dev only.
- Dedicated: can meet many networking and tenancy requirements (dedicated GPU pools, VPC peering) but our out-of-the-box Dedicated uses cloud KMS (AWS/GCP). We currently offer BYOK via cloud KMS and KMS keys can be customer-managed, but that is not the same as an on-prem HSM appliance. Some customers bridge with an HSM vendor gateway (e.g., vendor-provided cloud connector) — this can satisfy key custody requirements if the vendor supports remote attestation and the audit team accepts the vendor bridge. Need validation from Thales on supported topologies.
- Private: full feature match — supports customer-managed KMS/HSM appliances in-customer-VPC or on-prem, configurable log archival to customer storage with retention policies, and private networking (VPN/direct connect).

What we should prepare for Wed (deliverables):
1) Evidence pack (SOC 2 + network diagrams + retention options) — populate and send pre-read (redwood_evidence_pack_2026.zip).
2) HSM integration one-pager that lists supported topologies (appliance in customer VPC, HSM gateway, cloud-HSM BYOK) and known vendor compatibility notes (redwood_hsm_integration_onepager.pdf).
3) A short matrix comparing Dedicated vs Private for the specific CedarHealth asks (KMS custody, retention, network controls, expected timeline, procurement signals).
4) Cost range: rough order of magnitude (monthly) for Dedicated vs Private — we should provide a low/medium/high band to help procurement.

Technical owners to include on the call: Marissa (solutions eng) for deployment path + runbook; myself for commercial/fit; and engineering lead if there are deeper kernel/runtime questions.

I'll draft the Dedicated vs Private matrix and the cost buckets today and add to the Drive folder. Marissa — can you take the lead on the HSM topology doc? I can pull our previous Thales exchange for reference.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: infra constraints & hosting path — Wed 15 Dec deep-dive confirmed

Lisa — great, thanks for the quick turn. Wed 15 Dec 10:00 PT is on our side. Calendar invite coming from Aditya with a short agenda.

Pre-read and logistics:
- Pre-read folder (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/cedarhealth-redwood-evidence — we'll add the evidence pack and the HSM one-pager by EOD Mon.
- Attachments included: redwood_hsm_integration_onepager.pdf, redwood_evidence_pack_2026.zip (stubs in the folder for initial review).
- Ask for your team before the call: SAML IdP metadata, HSM admin contact (name/email), and any procurement constraints re: contract terms or data residency language they want visible up front.

On the Dedicated vs Private delta: Aditya and Marissa will give a short cost and timeline band during the meeting. My expectation to present to your security board (20 Dec) is that we will have enough to show the committee two viable options with pros/cons, and a recommended path (likely Private if on-prem HSM is required).

If anything changes on your side (e.g., ability to accept a vendor-managed HSM gateway), flag it in reply-all so we can adjust the prep.

Thanks — we'll be ready.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
